## AMEBIC LIVER ABSCESS
Serological testing for amoebiasis should be obtained in all patients with suspected amebic liver abscess. Multiple sets of anaerobic and aerobic blood cultures should also be obtained prior to starting antibiotics to exclude pyogenic liver abscess, which is a much more common cause of liver abscess.
Serologic testing can be negative in a small number of patients with acute presentation (symptoms <2 weeks). Repeat serology is usually positive. If repeat serological testing is negative for amoebiasis or patient does not respond to treatment of amebic liver abscess, patient should have further diagnostic testing completed to exclude pyogenic liver abscess.
Drainage of amebic liver abscess should be considered in patients with large lesions at risk of rupture.
Due to complicated treatment and follow up, Infectious Diseases consultation is recommended in all patients with liver abscess.
Treatment of patients with confirmed or suspected amebic liver abscess (obtain blood cultures prior to starting in suspected cases)
Paromomycin is nonformulary and must be ordered by Infectious Diseases.
Metronidazole 750 mg PO q8h for 10 days ($) [DI] <FOLLOWED BY> paromomycin 25-35 mg/kg/day PO q8h for 7 days ($) [M]
